children: US-based HR tech startup plans to expand its AI-led workforce automation platform across the US and Europe, with 80 per cent of its workforce based in Bengaluru

US-based HR technology startup Firstwork has raised USD 15 million (over Rs 142 crore) in a Series A funding round led by Earlybird Venture Capital to expand its AI-powered workforce automation platform across the US and Europe, as per a media report.

The round also saw participation from Legion VC and Deel Ventures, alongside existing investors Gradient and Y Combinator. The latest fundraise takes Firstwork’s total funding to USD 20 million since its launch in 2024.

The San Francisco-based startup plans to use the capital to expand its teams across applied AI, AI research, engineering and go-to-market functions. Around 80 per cent of its workforce operates from Bengaluru. The company also plans to strengthen its presence in the US and Europe and extend its AI agents to additional workforce operations.

Founded by former Deel executives Vardhan Kapoor and Shubham Choudhary, Firstwork uses AI agents to automate human resource operations for frontline workers. Its platform covers document verification, background checks, right-to-work checks, onboarding, training coordination, compliance management and worker follow-ups.
The platform integrates with existing HR systems, allowing employers to automate workflows without replacing their current software.

According to the company, more than 1.5 lakh frontline workers start work through its platform every month. Firstwork claims its technology can reduce the time spent by workers and HR teams on each new hire by up to 90 per cent. Its clients include Deel, Job&Talent, Relay, Wonolo and BGSF.

The fundraise comes amid increasing adoption of artificial intelligence across human resource functions. India's HR technology market is projected to grow to USD 2.3 billion by 2033 from USD 1.12 billion in 2024, according to industry estimates.

Several Indian startups are developing AI-based solutions for recruitment, onboarding and workforce management. Bengaluru-based Hunar.AI, which raised Rs 40 crore earlier this week, uses conversational AI agents to automate gig-worker hiring, onboarding, training and employee retention. Its clients include Swiggy, Zepto, Croma, Starbucks and Dr Lal PathLabs.

Hyderabad-based TurboHire raised USD 6 million in a Series A funding round led by IvyCap Ventures in August 2025 to expand its agentic AI-based recruitment platform. Founded in 2019, the startup automates enterprise hiring workflows and says it has onboarded more than 120 enterprises, including Cipla, Tata Motors, PwC, Lenskart and Britannia.

Other companies operating in adjacent segments include TraqCheck, which offers AI-powered background verification and recruitment agents, and HireBound, which automates candidate sourcing, screening and evaluation.
